name: Self-Fund It
blurb: Your money. Your board of one. Every dollar of upside stays here.
body: Nobody to answer to, nobody to bail you out. The budget comes out of the cash on hand right now, and if the launch is soft there is no cheque in the post to soften it.

name: Seed Term Sheet
blurb: They cover the build and wire again at launch — if the industry score clears the bar.
body: The term sheet is four pages and the word 'units' appears in none of them. What they want is a score, a photograph of you near a fern, and a slide they can put in front of their own investors. They recoup against unit sales, which is only a problem if you were planning to have any.

name: Growth Round
blurb: Much bigger advance, much bigger wire, and a score bar you will feel.
body: The partner who ran this round has a podcast about courage. Clear their bar and the launch wire is the largest number you have ever seen in one place. Miss it and they will still be supportive, publicly, at 40% of the wire. They recoup against unit sales, which is only a problem if you were planning to have any.

name: The Visionary Round
blurb: Enormous money against an enormous score. There is no third outcome.
body: They are not investing in a game, they are investing in a position. Hit their number or the wire collapses and the standing goes with it. Everyone in the room already knows you are going to sign it. They recoup against unit sales, which is only a problem if you were planning to have any.

name: Publishing Deal
blurb: They fund the build and the marketing. They take 30% and one slot.
body: The advance covers production, the marketing budget is real money you did not have to earn, and thirty cents of every dollar goes to a building in another country. One feature slot is theirs; you will find out which one at lock.

name: Platform Exclusive
blurb: A fat advance, an enormous marketing budget, 45% off the top, one storefront only.
body: One platform, one launch window, one very large cheque. The exclusivity halves your reach and the marketing spend more than covers it — on paper, in their model, which you have not been shown.

name: Boutique Label
blurb: Small advance, small cut, no mandated slot, and they actually play games.
body: Four people in a converted flat who have shipped nine things you respect. They will not make you rich and they will not make you add anything. Their festival contacts alone are worth the fifteen percent.

name: Ask The Players
blurb: No board, no publisher. The advance is whatever your audience trusts you for.
body: You film the pitch in front of the CRT and you do not lie once. What comes back is a direct function of how many people you have not let down yet — and every one of them now owns a small piece of your conscience.
